items.title: Why Southwest Airlines Isn’t Rejecting Early Boeing 737 MAX 7s Like 777X Airlines Did
items.summary: Boeing's long-delayed 777X program has encountered an unusual problem: some of its largest customers do not want the aircraft it built first. Emirates has rejected its earliest examples, while Lufthansa is negotiating over which aircraft it will accept. The issue is the extensive modifications necessary to bring older airframes up to current production standards, following years of development and certification delays.
items.t: Why Southwest Airlines Isn’t Rejecting Early Boeing 737 MAX 7s Like 777X Airlines Did

items.title: flydubai Cleared To Return To Israel 2 Months After Boeing 737 Hijack Attempt
items.summary: Earlier this year, a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight was the subject of a hijacking by one of its own pilots. While his efforts were thwarted, with fellow flydubai pilots traveling on board the service able to regain control and divert the jet to Saudi Arabia , it prompted a strong response, with Israeli authorities banning the airline until at least mid-December. Now, however, the carrier has been granted approval to return.
items.t: flydubai Cleared To Return To Israel 2 Months After Boeing 737 Hijack Attempt

items.title: Aviation security’s next blind spot: The threat from within
items.summary:
Amir Lezer is Chief Security Officer at Avia Solutions Group, with three decades of experience in aviation security, intelligence, investigations, and enterprise risk management. His career includes service as an air marshal and aviation security manager in government service, and senior security leadership roles in multinational organizations. 

The views and opinions expressed in this column are solely those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the official policy or position of Avia Solutions Group or AeroTime. 

On September 30, 2026, a passenger flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia after a violent struggle on the flight deck . According to the UAE attorney general, the co-pilot had begun carrying out a planned terrorist attack: to take control of the aircraft and fly it into the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport. The aircraft lost thousands of feet before the captain, wounded in the attack, managed in an act of real courage to open the cockpit door. Passengers forced their way in, restrained the co-pilot and helped stabilize the aircraft, which then landed safely. 

The alleged attacker did not slip past a screening checkpoint. He was a licensed pilot, sitting in the cockpit with every right to be there. After three decades in aviation security, including years as an air marshal, I believe this is the question our industry must now answer: 

For 25 years we have worked to keep threats out of the cockpit. Are we prepared for one that is already inside it? 

How fast 9/11 changed everything  

Until 2001, aviation security was built…
items.t: Aviation security’s next blind spot: The threat from within

The company announced this month that it would cut 5% of the roughly 50,000 employees in its commercial airplanes division, and now expects to reach 47 jets a month in early 2027, according to Reuters.

items.title: Xiamen Airlines signs deal for 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft
items.summary:
Xiamen Airlines, a subsidiary of China Southern Airlines, signed an agreement with Boeing on November 24, 2026, to purchase 50 737-8 (737 MAX 8) aircraft, according to a stock exchange filing China Southern published the same day.

The filing puts the combined list price of the 50 jets, including airframes and engines, at approximately $7.4 billion. China Southern said Boeing had granted Xiamen Airlines a significant discount but did not disclose the actual purchase price.

The aircraft are scheduled for delivery in batches between 2031 and 2034. Xiamen Airlines will make advance payments, with the balance for each aircraft due upon delivery. The carrier will finance the purchase through its own funds, capital-raising proceeds and bank loans, according to the filing.

The agreement remains subject to approval from China Southern’s shareholders and the relevant Chinese government authorities.

Xiamen Airlines prepares for new airport hub 

China Southern’s board linked the purchase to Xiamen Airlines’ upcoming relocation to Xiamen Xiang’an International Airport, the development of its hub network in Fujian province and the optimization of its fleet.

The new airport is scheduled to open by the end of 2026, replacing Xiamen Gaoqi International Airport (XMN).

China Southern owns a 55% stake in Xiamen Airlines, which operated an all-Boeing fleet before it placed its first Airbus order in September 2022 .

On April 29, 2026, Xiamen Airlines also agreed to purchase 35 A320neo-family aircraft for delivery between 2029 and 2032, as part of a 137-aircraft group order with a…
items.t: Xiamen Airlines signs deal for 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft

items.title: Russian warplanes trigger unprecedented air raid alert in South Korea
items.summary:
South Korea issued an unprecedented air raid alert for Ulleung County on November 24, 2026, after several Russian military aircraft entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) over the Sea of Japan, known in South Korea as the East Sea, and approached the island of Ulleungdo, according to the country’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS). 

The JCS said it had detected the Russian aircraft before they entered the zone and that they subsequently turned away without violating South Korean territorial airspace. The Republic of Korea Air Force (ROKAF) scrambled fighter jets in response, with South Korean media reporting that F-15Ks were among the aircraft deployed. 

Local media citing military officials put the number of Russian aircraft at fewer than five. The JCS did not identify the aircraft types or disclose how long they remained in the zone or how close they came to South Korean territorial airspace. 

Residents ordered to take shelter  

At the military’s request, South Korea’s Ministry of the Interior and Safety issued an air raid alert at 07:52 local time. A minute later, it sent an emergency text message instructing residents to seek shelter underground or indoors. The message incorrectly reported that Russian aircraft had violated South Korean airspace. The alert was lifted within five minutes. 

Further confusion arose when North Gyeongsang Province’s all-clear message referred to a suspected North Korean aircraft. Provincial authorities said they had mistakenly reused a template from a civil defense drill, changing only the time. 

JCS spokesperson Captain…
items.t: Russian warplanes trigger unprecedented air raid alert in South Korea

items.title: Ryanair promises major German expansion if Merz scraps ‘damaging’ taxes and fees
items.summary:
Ryanair has promised a major German expansion, including more aircraft and routes, if the government scraps ‘damaging’ taxes and fees.

On November 24, 2026, Ryanair’s CEO Michael O’Leary was in Germany to unveil a $3.6 billion growth plan for Germany on the condition that Chancellor Friedrich Merz abolishes Germany’s “harmful” air passenger duty and reduces the “astronomically high access costs”.

In return, Ryanair said it would double its passenger volume in Germany from 17 million to 34 million per year, station 36 new Boeing 737 MAX aircraft in the country, expand its route network to over 550 connections, open new bases in cities such as Düsseldorf, Dortmund, Hamburg, and Stuttgart, and create more than 1,000 direct jobs in Germany by 2032.

O’Leary claimed Germany has the “worst-recovered air transport market in Europe after the Covid pandemic” and made air travel “hopelessly uncompetitive with astronomically high taxes as well as airport, air traffic control, and security fees”.

Ryanair 

“Chancellor Merz is right when he says that Germany is harming itself with this damaging air traffic tax because traffic is being shifted from Germany to countries like Slovakia, Sweden, Italy, and Poland, which have abolished the air traffic tax and reduced access costs,” O’Leary added. “Why doesn’t he adopt this successful approach?”

In a press release accompanying O’Leary’s visit, the Irish carrier said it was offering the Merz government a “unique opportunity to revive Germany’s collapsing air travel market and boost the sluggish German economy”.

On November 3, 2026,…
items.t: Ryanair promises major German expansion if Merz scraps ‘damaging’ taxes and fees

items.title: AirAsia says worst is over as Q3 losses halve, months after bailout rumors
items.summary:
AirAsia Group says it has turned a corner after a turbulent year marked by soaring fuel prices, deep capacity cuts and questions over its financial state.

Releasing its third-quarter results on November 23, 2026, the Malaysian low-cost group reported that its net loss had more than halved compared with the previous quarter, while its operating earnings rose sharply. 

The improvement came even though July to September is typically the slowest period of the year for airlines in the region, coinciding with the monsoon season in markets such as Thailand and the Philippines.

“Our third quarter performance suggests that the worst is behind us,” said AirAsia Group CEO Bo Lingam.

Fewer flights, higher fares 

The recovery has come from flying less, but more profitably. AirAsia cut capacity by about a quarter compared with a year earlier, trimming flights at off-peak times and dropping routes that were losing money. Revenue fell, but by far less than the capacity cuts, as average fares rose by almost a quarter and planes stayed about 80% full.

Higher fares and surcharges, along with tighter cost controls, allowed the group to recover about 75% of its higher fuel bill. Jet fuel averaged US$152 per barrel in the quarter, down from a peak of US$183 in the second quarter but still well above pre-crisis levels.

“By trimming unviable capacity and enforcing strict fare discipline, we pushed RASK up 20% while keeping load factors healthy,” Lingam said, referring to revenue per available seat kilometer, a key measure of airline earnings. He said travelers are favoring shorter,…
items.t: AirAsia says worst is over as Q3 losses halve, months after bailout rumors

items.title: Incora’s Willis Lee on why going local is the key to APAC supply chain certainty
items.summary:
As airlines and maintenance providers across Asia Pacific contend with fleet growth, tight parts supply and long lead times, aerospace supply chain specialist Incora has built up its presence on the ground in the region.

The company, which supplies hardware, chemicals and supply chain management services to the aerospace and defense industries, opened a new office in Johor, Malaysia, in November 2025. The facility houses Incora’s Asia Pacific Shared Service Center, which supports more than 250 customers and 300 vendors across the region.

During MRO Asia-Pacific 2026 in Singapore, AeroTime spoke exclusively with Willis Lee, Business Development Director for Asia Pacific at Incora, about what running the business locally means for customers, and why the company is investing now, before the demand fully arrives.

Why Incora sees itself as a supply chain partner, not a parts broker 

Incora describes itself as an integrated supply chain partner rather than a parts distributor or broker. Lee said the difference shows up most clearly on the customer’s shop floor.

“In practice, what we do is we actually deploy people on site to support the customer, to help them manage demand, supply, forecasting, planning, and also to manage our localized stock,” he said. “That’s a major difference, especially for MRO customers.”

The company has amassed more than 20 years of experience working with major MROs and OEMs. Because it handles demand across its entire global network, Incora can also offer more competitive pricing on traditional supply.

Lee said customers in Asia also expect a…
items.t: Incora’s Willis Lee on why going local is the key to APAC supply chain certainty

items.title: Boeing moves closer to 737 MAX deliveries from new North Line at Everett
items.summary:
Boeing has moved a step closer to customer deliveries of 737 aircraft built at its new North Line facility in Everett, Washington, according to The Air Current.

On November 23, 2026, The Air Current reported that Everett-built 737s had been added to Boeing’s PC700 production certificate, marking a key regulatory milestone for the new North Line.

Boeing announced that the first 737 MAX manufactured in Everett had rolled off the assembly line in October 2026, marking the first time narrowbodies have been built at the factory.

Since the assembly line was first opened in July 2026, Boeing has focused on low-rate initial production and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) conformities as the planemaker progressed towards adding Everett-built 737s to its production certificate.

Boeing 

The FAA conducted additional inspections on the first several aircraft built on the line, ensuring that they are produced in the same way as they are in Renton.

According to The Air Current, which spoke with people with knowledge of developments at Boeing, the planemaker is currently moving through the final steps of the FAA audit.

Boeing’s fourth production line is already filling up with additional 737 MAXs including the recently approved MAX 10.

The space in Everett is larger than Renton with the North Line able to accommodate the longer 737-10 in every factory position.

The factory had available space after the end of 747 production and the consolidation of 787 final assembly in South Carolina.

New Boeing North Line will play key role in 737 production ramp up

items.t: Boeing moves closer to 737 MAX deliveries from new North Line at Everett

items.title: NATO to deploy AWACS aircraft as Russian airspace violations in Poland continue
items.summary:
NATO will forward-deploy one of its Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft following the incursion of three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles into Polish airspace on November 20, 2026, the alliance announced after a meeting of the North Atlantic Council in Brussels. 

The announcement came shortly before Poland reported another violation of its airspace by a Russian drone on November 23, 2026, prompting its military to authorize the use of weapons before ultimately deciding against shooting down the aircraft. 

In a statement , NATO spokesperson Allison Hart said Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR) General Alexus Grynkewich had authorized the deployment and was considering sending additional assets as part of an ongoing review of the alliance’s deterrence and defense posture in Poland and elsewhere. 

“This was a dangerous incident and Russia bears full responsibility,” the statement said. NATO did not specify where the aircraft would be based or how long it would remain deployed. 

Poland seeks additional NATO air defense assets  

Speaking to reporters in Brussels after the meeting, Polish Deputy Defence Minister Paweł Zalewski said the AWACS aircraft would be made available to Poland and that Warsaw had requested additional aircraft from its allies. 

Unlike in September 2025, when a large-scale Russian drone incursion prompted Warsaw to invoke Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty, Poland opted to seek additional allied military support without triggering formal consultations under the treaty provision. 

Zalewski added that further Polish proposals…
items.t: NATO to deploy AWACS aircraft as Russian airspace violations in Poland continue

items.title: GE Aerospace defense CEO to leave firm after four years
items.summary:
The President and CEO of GE Aerospace Defense and Systems is stepping down from her role in 2027 after over four years at the company.

On November 23, 2026, GE Aerospace said that Amy Gowder would depart in the first quarter of 2027 to “pursue external opportunities”.

Gowder joined GE Aerospace as the CEO of its defense unit in April 2022, after two years as the COO at Aerojet Rockedyne and more than a decade at Lockheed Martin .

Darin DiTommaso, Vice President of Engineering for Defense and Systems, will immediately assume the role of interim president and CEO while GE Aerospace searches for a permanent replacement.

“Amy has played an integral role in building our Defense business as we prepared for and launched GE Aerospace as a standalone public company,” said GE Aerospace Chairman and CEO, H. Lawrence Culp, Jr. “Throughout her time with us, the team has grown orders, increased engine deliveries to customers, and progressed next-generation programs. We are grateful for her leadership at GE Aerospace.”

DiTommaso is a GE Aerospace veteran having joined the company over 37 years ago and has since held a variety of positions across commercial and defense operations.

DiTommaso led GE Aerospace’s performance and preliminary design teams across several engine programs, including GEnx, LEAP, Honda, and Passport.

He also led teams on the program that laid the groundwork for the XA100 adaptive-cycle military engine.

“With more than three decades at GE Aerospace building some of our most advanced commercial and military aircraft, Darin DiTommaso knows our business deeply…
items.t: GE Aerospace defense CEO to leave firm after four years

items.title: Sheltair and APP Jet Center to combine in 23-location FBO deal
items.summary:
Sheltair and APP Jet Center have agreed to combine operations in a deal that will create a 23-location fixed-base operator network. The combined business will use the Sheltair name and be led by APP Jet Center CEO Mark Johnstone. Financial terms were not disclosed.

Sheltair operates 17 locations, including 14 in Florida and facilities in Savannah, Georgia; Denton, Texas; and Broomfield, Colorado. It manages more than 4.7 million square feet of aviation-related property.

Founded in 1963 by Jerry Holland, Sheltair remained family-owned until Bain Capital acquired it from the Holland family. Lisa Holland, Jerry’s daughter and Sheltair’s President and CEO, said she had focused on finding a new owner to carry on the family’s legacy.

The combination follows Bain’s January 2026 acquisition of APP Jet Center, then a five-location operator. Bain said it planned to grow the business through acquisitions and investments in facilities, particularly hangar capacity at airports where space is limited. Johnstone, formerly CEO of Signature Aviation, will lead the larger platform.

The deal is part of a broader shift in FBO ownership. Private-equity firms and other investment funds have become increasingly active buyers, as financially backed groups now account for a larger share of interested buyers in smaller FBO transactions than traditional aviation operators.

The largest operators are also attracting major investors. In August, Apollo-managed funds acquired a significant interest in Atlantic Aviation, while KKR remained a substantial shareholder. The transaction valued Atlantic at…
items.t: Sheltair and APP Jet Center to combine in 23-location FBO deal

items.title: Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite by year-end, German media report
items.summary:
Western intelligence agencies believe Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit in December 2026, according to a joint investigation by German broadcasters NDR and WDR and the newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung.

The satellite, identified in the reporting as Sputnik-S, was reportedly built several years ago and stored in the Moscow region. Intelligence warnings circulated in early November 2026 said it could be launched within 60 days. Germany’s Space Command reportedly assesses that a launch could happen within weeks. The reports say the satellite could become operational soon after reaching orbit.

The claims are based on intelligence shared among some NATO member states, including information held by Germany’s foreign intelligence service, the BND, and its armed forces.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance continually assesses its defense posture and security in space. Chancellor Friedrich Merz called the reports shocking.

A US Defense Intelligence Agency report published in October says Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon for use against other satellites.

A nuclear detonation in orbit could damage or disable satellites across low Earth orbit, disrupting communications, navigation and other services. US Space Command chief Stephen Whiting has estimated that about one-third of satellites in low Earth orbit could fail within hours or days, with further failures over the following months.

Placing a nuclear weapon in orbit would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which prohibits weapons of mass destruction in…
items.t: Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite by year-end, German media report

items.title: Trump predicts 250 more Boeing jets for China as earlier pledge still pending
items.summary:
US President Donald Trump said he expects China to buy another 250 Boeing aircraft, days after meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China.

The prediction comes as the status of a separate 200-aircraft commitment announced in May 2026 has yet to be publicly clarified.

“I think they’re going to do another 250,” Trump said in an interview with CNBC. He did not identify the aircraft models, delivery schedule or possible airlines involved. Boeing did not immediately comment, nor has China discussed plans for additional Boeing jets.

The earlier 200-aircraft commitment was announced during Trump’s May 2026 visit to China. Boeing at the time described it as an initial commitment, not a finalized order.

Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said China would allocate aircraft to individual airlines, after which Boeing would negotiate firm orders with each carrier. Boeing does not include preliminary commitments in its official order backlog.

In September 2026, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said China was making progress on that earlier commitment. He said about 140 aircraft were “in a good state” and orders for another 10 were being written.

Trump said in May that the initial commitment could eventually grow to as many as 750 aircraft.

The prospect of a larger order comes amid a renewed effort by Boeing to regain ground in China. The company had been largely shut out of the market since 2017, while Airbus expanded its position. China is expected to need thousands of new aircraft in coming decades.

Earlier Boeing talks with China have also been tied to the…
items.t: Trump predicts 250 more Boeing jets for China as earlier pledge still pending

items.title: Spain’s Plus Ultra may have operated final flight, ceased operations
items.summary:
Spanish long-haul airline Plus Ultra Líneas Aéreas appeared to have completely ceased operations on November 23, 2026. 

The previous day, what may have been its final flight, PU711, operated by an Airbus A330-200 aircraft, took off from Caracas (CCS), Venezuela, at around 20.00 local time bound for Madrid-Barajas (MAD), with an intermediate stop at Tenerife Norte (TFN). 

While the aircraft was in the air, the airline’s website stopped accepting new bookings, according to reports published by a number of Spanish media outlets. 

The troubled carrier filed for preliminary creditor protection just a few days earlier and announced the discontinuation of all its scheduled operations except for those linking Spain to Venezuela.  

It is not clear whether the cessation of scheduled operations will also affect the charter and ACMI business. Plus Ultra had previously highlighted its intention to focus on that part of the business, although the sudden and unannounced end to its Venezuela operations has raised doubts about this possibility. 

As of November 2026, Plus Ultra employs approximately 670 people and operates a fleet of seven Airbus A330 aircraft. 

Spanish media has also reported that vertically integrated tour operator Ávoris could be interested in acquiring Plus Ultra’s assets. Ávoris already operates its own in-house airline, Iberojet, which operates leisure-oriented scheduled services linking Spain and Portugal to several destinations in the Americas and Asia. 

AeroTime has contacted Plus Ultra for comment.

The post Spain’s Plus Ultra may have operated final…

items.title: Ukrainian Mirage 2000 shoots down jet-powered drone with cannon: video
items.summary:
The Ukrainian Air Force has released footage of one of its French-supplied Mirage 2000 fighters shooting down a jet-powered drone with its 30 mm cannon. 

The video comes as Kyiv and its partners work to secure more aircraft gun ammunition to counter faster Russian attack drones.

The Ukrainian Air Force did not identify the drone type or say when or where the interception took place.

Guns on target.
Ukrainian Mirage 2000 takes down a jet-powered drone. https://t.co/fQ3ZVwNODa

— Ukrainian Air Force (@KpsZSU) November 23, 2026 

Mirage 2000 cannon offers alternative to air-to-air missiles 

Ukraine operates the Mirage 2000-5F variant, equipped with two internal 30 mm DEFA 554 cannons. France delivered the first aircraft on February 6, 2025 , and Ukraine first reported using them in combat against Russian cruise missiles a month later.

Ukraine’s Mirage 2000s also carry short-range, infrared-guided R550 Magic 2 missiles and medium-range MICA air-to-air missiles. The latter were first publicly documented on Ukrainian aircraft in January 2026 , expanding their ability to engage targets at greater distances.

Cannon fire allows pilots to destroy drones without expending air-to-air missiles, but requires closing to short range. That brings considerable risks: a drone’s warhead may detonate when hit, sending fragments into the fighter’s flight path that can damage the aircraft or be ingested by its engine.

On October 12, 2022, a Ukrainian MiG-29 crashed while intercepting Russian drones in the Vinnytsia region. According to Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation , one…
items.t: Ukrainian Mirage 2000 shoots down jet-powered drone with cannon: video

items.title: JSX to bring New Pacific Airways back into operation after bankruptcy
items.summary:
JSX, a private charter operator based in Dallas, Texas, has acquired New Pacific Airways (NPA), a failed startup airline which ceased operations in November 2025 and subsequently filed for bankruptcy in January 2026. 

With this acquisition, JSX has secured a Part 121 air carrier certificate (air operator certificate or AOC in ICAO’s terminology), which allows it to operate as a conventional scheduled airline. 

Until now, JSX has been flying under the Part 135 regulatory framework. This set up has several advantages, such as enabling the use of private terminals and lighter crew and operational requirements, but it has also limited JSX to using aircraft with no more than 30 seats. 

According to several media reports, the acquisition of New Pacific Airlines was closed back in August 2026, but the news has only just been made public when JSX filed a request with the US Department of Transportation (DOT) to use NPA’s AOC to operate several of its services. 

JSX intends to operate at least six Embraer E145 aircraft fitted with 42 seats under the newly acquired airline’s air operator certificate. 

If the request is approved, this would see the comeback, even if under a different brand, of a carrier that has gone through several business model iterations since launching publicly in January 2021. 

At first, New Pacific Airways intended to operate a B757 scheduled service between the continental United States and East Asia by way of Alaska. However, the plan never came to fruition due to protracted issues with the obtention of flight permits. Consequently, NPA switched to…
items.t: JSX to bring New Pacific Airways back into operation after acquisition

items.title: Dutch F-35As and French Rafales operate from Finnish highway strip
items.summary:
Dutch F-35As and French Rafales have operated from the Jännevirta highway strip in eastern Finland during Protective Fence 26, the Finnish Air Force’s main exercise of the year, as NATO allies practice dispersing their fighters away from conventional air bases. 

The Dutch Ministry of Defense said on November 20, 2026 , that several F-35As had landed on Highway 9 near Kuopio that day. 

The Finnish Air Force reported that French Rafales deployed to Rovaniemi had carried out touch-and-go landings at the same location, marking the first time the French fighter had operated from a Finnish highway. 

The French Air and Space Force identified the participating Rafales as aircraft from the fighter test and evaluation squadron ECE 1/30 “Côte d’Argent.” 

The Jännevirta strip sits on Highway 9 near Rissala Air Base, home of the Finnish Air Force’s Karelia Air Wing. The road is closed to civilian traffic from November 18 to 25, 2026. 

NATO fighters disperse across Finland during Protective Fence 26  

Protective Fence 26 runs from November 19 to 27, 2026, involving more than 40 aircraft and about 4,100 personnel, including some 1,800 reservists. 

The Finnish Air Force has deployed 20 F/A-18 Hornets across military bases, civilian airports and highway strips . The Dutch F-35As operate from Rissala, the French Rafales from Rovaniemi, while Swedish Gripens are based at Kallax Air Base in northern Sweden. 

Finland’s own F-35As, the first two of which arrived at Rovaniemi in September 2026 , are not taking part. 

The exercise focuses on Agile Combat Employment (ACE), a concept aimed…
items.t: Dutch F-35As and French Rafales operate from Finnish highway strip

items.title: Inside Joramco’s expansion: New hangars, smarter maintenance and global ambitions
items.summary:
Joramco is preparing for its next phase of expansion, building on the success of Hangar 7 with two additional hangars planned in Jordan, a growing pipeline of aircraft maintenance engineers and new digital technologies designed to make its operations more efficient.

Speaking to AeroTime at MRO Europe in Amsterdam, held from October 27 to 29, 2026, Fraser Currie, Chief Strategy and Commercial Officer at DAE Engineering, outlined how the company intends to build on its growing international presence while keeping workforce development and safety at the heart of its strategy.

“Our growth strategy is based on what our customers are asking for,” Currie said. “We could have built three hangars at the same time, but would we have been able to control our expansion through the people? No, we would have lost something in that process.”

Currie was appointed Chief Strategy and Commercial Officer at DAE Engineering after serving as Chief Executive Officer of Joramco from October 2021 to September 2025. DAE Engineering is the engineering division of Dubai Aerospace Enterprise (DAE), under which Joramco operates.

Two more hangars in Joramco’s expansion plan 

Hangar 7 at Queen Alia International Airport (AMM), inaugurated by his H.M King Abdullah II on September 8, 2025, can accommodate aircraft up to the size of the Airbus A380 and increased Joramco’s capacity from 17 to 25 maintenance lines, according to the company.

Currie said MRO capacity remains in short supply, with about 60% of Joramco’s business coming from Europe and the remaining 40% from the wider region.

items.t: Inside Joramco’s expansion: New hangars, smarter maintenance and global ambitions

items.title: French Navy receives third Falcon 2000 Albatros maritime surveillance aircraft
items.summary:
France’s defense procurement agency, the Direction générale de l’armement (DGA), delivered a third Dassault Falcon 2000 Albatros maritime surveillance and intervention aircraft to the French Navy on November 16, 2026, completing the three deliveries scheduled for this year. 

In a statement published on November 19, 2026 , the DGA said the aircraft was destined for Flottille 24F at Lann-Bihoué naval air base in Brittany, where the first two Albatros arrived on July 27 and 31, 2026 . The agency confirmed that deliveries would continue at a rate of two aircraft per year. 

Falcon Albatros to replace two aging surveillance fleets  

The Albatros is a militarized version of Dassault Aviation’s Falcon 2000LXS business jet, acquired under France’s Maritime Surveillance and Intervention Aircraft (AVSIMAR) program. The DGA ordered seven aircraft in December 2020 and five more in September 2025 , bringing the total to 12. 

The new aircraft will replace eight Falcon 50M surveillance jets based in Brittany and five Falcon 200 Gardian aircraft stationed in the Pacific. According to the DGA, the retirement of both older types began in 2025. 

Designed for maritime surveillance, search and rescue, and other missions supporting French operations at sea, the Albatros offers an operational radius 10% to 30% greater than the aircraft it is replacing, according to the DGA. 

Its main sensors include a Thales SearchMaster X-band active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar and a Safran EuroFLIR 410 electro-optical turret, both integrated through a mission system developed by Naval Group.…
items.t: French Navy receives third Falcon 2000 Albatros maritime surveillance aircraft

items.title: Canada’s Scout fighter drone gains 12 partners, including Pratt & Whitney
items.summary:
Ottawa-based Dominion Dynamics has enlisted 12 aerospace and defense companies, including Pratt & Whitney Canada, Telesat and Thales Canada, to help develop Scout, an uncrewed combat aircraft designed to fly alongside crewed fighter jets, the company announced on November 20, 2026. 

According to the company’s statement , the other nine partners are Top Aces, ITPS Canada, PV Labs, SRC Can, Altitude Aerospace, Groupe DCM, HSB Solutions, North Aircraft Industries and RAMPF Composite Solutions. 

Dominion describes Scout as Canada’s first Autonomous Collaborative Platform (ACP), a type of uncrewed combat aircraft comparable to those being developed under the US Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program . 

The announcement does not specify what each company will contribute. Collectively, the partners bring expertise in aircraft structures and composites, landing gear, avionics, flight controls, engines, sensors and secure communications, as well as flight testing, training, maintenance and fleet management. 

Dominion said specialized suppliers from other NATO countries would complement the Canadian consortium. 

“The next generation of military aircraft will evolve at the speed of software. Canada has a chance to build that generation here,” said Eliot Pence, founder and CEO of Dominion Dynamics. 

Pratt & Whitney engine and Telesat satellite link for Scout  

Dominion announced that Scout would be powered by a Canadian-built Pratt & Whitney Canada PW300-series turbofan, an engine family widely used on business jets. The company said Scout’s airframe was being…
items.t: Canada’s Scout fighter drone gains 12 partners, including Pratt & Whitney

items.title: LATAM Airlines unveils cabin interiors for its upcoming A321XLR fleet
items.summary:
LATAM Airlines has officially unveiled the cabin design for its upcoming Airbus A321XLR fleet. 

While some elements of the new cabins had already been disclosed in April 2026 , on November 18, 2026, the airline’s CEO, Roberto Alvo , shared a video on LinkedIn , which depicted what the cabin of the new aircraft will look like. 

The aircraft will be configured to carry 174 passengers and will include 12 Premium Business suites and 162 seats in Economy, 36 of which will be more spacious. 

The Premium Business cabin, a first for this type of aircraft in the region, will be fitted with Thompson Aero Seating VantageSOLO full lie-flat suites in a 1-1 layout, which offers direct aisle access, as well as privacy doors. Each suite will feature a 19-inch OLED screen and wireless charging stations. 

The two suites in the first row will feature extra space, a larger screen, and additional space to leave hand luggage within the suite, rather than in the overhead bins. 

The Economy cabin will be arranged in a standard 3-3 configuration and be fitted with reclinable Recaro R3 state-of-the-art seats with flexible headrests. Each seat will also feature a 13-inch OLED screen as well as USB-C power outlets to recharge personal electronic devices. 

Passengers on LATAM’s A321XLR fleet will also enjoy internet connectivity provided by satellite operator SES. Earlier in 2026, the Latin American carrier announced that it would be allocating US$25 million to bring internet to 60 of its narrowbody aircraft, including new aircraft and retrofits. 

LATAM has 13 A321XLRs on order, which are…
items.t: LATAM Airlines unveils cabin interiors for its upcoming A321XLR fleet

items.title: Ukraine presses Sweden for faster Gripen jets delivery and Meteor missiles
items.summary:
Ukraine’s Minister of Defence Evgeniy Khmara has urged Sweden to accelerate the transfer of Saab Gripen fighters to Ukraine and ensure they arrive with the weapons needed for combat, particularly Meteor long-range air-to-air missiles. 

According to a readout published by Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence on November 22, 2026, Khmara met with General Michael Claesson, Supreme Commander of the Swedish Armed Forces, to discuss the next steps in transferring the aircraft, equipping them with weapons and finding ways to speed up deliveries. 

Ukraine wants Meteor missiles to counter Russian glide-bomb carriers  

An MBDA Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile on static display. (Credit: AeroTime) 

Khmara said Ukraine is counting on Gripen fighters to strengthen its air defenses, particularly against jet-powered drones and Russian aircraft carrying glide bombs. 

He stressed that weapons must arrive alongside the fighters, singling out Meteor missiles as a priority for countering Russian aviation. With a range exceeding 200 kilometers (124 miles) and a ramjet engine that maintains thrust throughout its flight, Meteor can engage enemy aircraft at long distances, potentially forcing Russian glide-bomb carriers to release their weapons farther from Ukrainian airspace. 

Ukraine also raised its need for aircraft cannon ammunition, with the two sides discussing whether Sweden could supply it.

items.t: Ukraine presses Sweden for faster Gripen jets delivery and Meteor missiles

items.title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury orbit after nearly eight years in space
items.summary:
The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission has entered orbit around Mercury, completing a nearly eight-year journey to the Solar System’s innermost planet.

The European Space Agency (ESA) confirmed the successful orbital capture on November 21, 2026, after its mission control team received signals from the spacecraft and assessed the initial telemetry.

The manoeuvre involved firing four thrusters on ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) to reduce the spacecraft’s speed enough for Mercury’s gravity to capture it. BepiColombo initially entered an elliptical polar orbit measuring approximately 590 by 11,640 kilometres.

Launched in October 2018, BepiColombo has travelled around 9.9 billion kilometres through the inner Solar System and completed nine planetary flybys: one of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury.

Two orbiters travelling together 

BepiColombo is a joint mission between ESA and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). It consists of two scientific spacecraft: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, known as Mio.

The two orbiters are currently still connected and travelling together. Mio remains protected by a sunshield, while MPO is responsible for the spacecraft stack’s manoeuvres during the final stages of arrival.

The orbiters are scheduled to separate on December 9–10, 2026. Mio will then move into its planned orbit to study Mercury’s magnetic field and magnetosphere, while MPO will perform additional manoeuvres to reach its own final science orbit.

items.t: BepiColombo reaches Mercury orbit after nearly eight years in space

items.title: Drones strike Russian military-linked cargo ship in Gulf of Finland
items.summary:
A Russian cargo ship linked to the country’s military logistics network caught fire after a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland on November 21, 2026. The damaged vessel drifted into Finnish territorial waters, where authorities coordinated a rescue and firefighting operation involving Finnish, Estonian and Russian units.

The ship, Sparta II, was sailing from St. Petersburg toward Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave when it was hit. Finnish military officials said Ukraine was likely behind the attack, although Kyiv had not publicly claimed responsibility.

Drone attack damages ship 

Finnish Defence Forces detected a drone attack against the Russian cargo vessel on November 21, 2026, west of Gogland Island in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

Estonia’s Police and Border Guard Board said the explosions occurred while the ship was in Estonia’s exclusive economic zone, outside its territorial waters, in an international shipping lane. Finnish authorities initially described the attack location as international waters.

Russian officials said two drones struck the vessel. Finnish authorities confirmed a drone attack but did not independently confirm the number of drones involved.

The strike damaged the ship and started a fire. The vessel subsequently lost its ability to maneuver and drifted north into Finnish waters, eventually anchoring off the coastal town of Loviisa.

items.t: Drones strike Russian military-linked cargo ship in Gulf of Finland

items.title: Belgian strike to disrupt flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports
items.summary:
Brussels Airport (BRU) expects major flight disruption on November 23, after some air traffic controllers at Belgian air navigation service provider skeyes announced they would join a national demonstration.

The airport said most arriving and departing flights will have to be cancelled because skeyes will not be able to provide normal air traffic control services during the action. The disruption is expected from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. local time (6 a.m. – 8 p.m. UTC).

Skeyes unable to provide normal ATC services 

According to Skeyes, the expected number of staff would not be enough to safely handle regular air traffic during the strike. It will therefore temporarily suspend normal services at Belgian airports and in the airspace under its responsibility. Minimum services will be maintained for emergency and other safety-critical flights.

Brussels Airport said airlines will contact affected passengers directly. Flight cancellations will appear on the airport’s website once they have been registered by the carriers.

Charleroi Airport also expects flights to stop 

The disruption will also affect Brussels South Charleroi Airport (CRL), another major Belgian airport and an important base for low-cost airlines.

Charleroi Airport said no flights will be able to take off or land between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m. on the same day because ATC will not be available during that period.

The airport said it had arranged staffing to keep its own operations running, while respecting employees’ right to join the demonstration. However, without air traffic control, aircraft cannot operate safely.…
items.t: Belgian strike to disrupt flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports
